slides.title: Who owns it?
slides.text:
We add **'s** to a name or noun to show who **has** something.

**Ali's** bag = the bag that Ali has
the **cat's** bowl = the bowl the cat has

slides.title: The little mark
slides.text:
The mark **'** is called an **apostrophe**.

It goes **before** the s when there is **one** owner.

the **girl's** hat
my **dad's** car

slides.title: Not every s
slides.text:
Do **not** add an apostrophe just because a word ends in s.

I have two **cats**. (more than one)
The **cat's** tail is long. (the tail the cat has)

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Ask: does someone **own** or **have** the thing?
2. If yes, look for the **'s**.
3. Find another word in the text with 's. It shows the same rule.

sentences.t: The bird's cage is by the window.

example.explain:
**bird's** cage: the cage the bird has.
**Omar's** sister: the sister Omar has.

One owner, so **'s**.

together.passage: Huda has a little sister named Lama. ___ doll has a pink dress. Lama's bed is next to the window. Huda's books are on the shelf.
together.hint: The doll belongs to Lama. One owner gets apostrophe + s.
together.good: Yes! The doll is Lama's, so we write **Lama's**.

sentences: Huda has a little sister named Lama.
Lama's bed is next to the window.
Huda's books are on the shelf.
evidence.stem: The answer was: Lama's. Tap 2 sentences that also use 's to show who owns something.
evidence.wrong: This sentence has no word with 's. Look for a name with an apostrophe.

checks.passage: The ___ ball went over the wall.
checks.stem: Which word fills the blank? (one boy)
checks.why: The ball belongs to one boy, so we add **'s**: **boy's**.

checks.passage: My mom's car is white. My dads car is blue.
checks.why: The car belongs to Dad. It should be **dad's** car.

checks.passage: I see three ___ in the tree.
checks.why: Nobody owns anything here. There are just many birds, so **no apostrophe**.

again.title: Turn it around
again.text:
Say it the long way: **the ___ of ___**.

If it works, use 's.
again.example:
the toy of the baby → the **baby's** toy

the house of Sara → **Sara's** house

slides.title: One owner
slides.text:
For **one** owner, add **'s**.

the **teacher's** desk (one teacher)
the **horse's** saddle (one horse)

slides.title: Many owners
slides.text:
For **many** owners, the noun usually already ends in **s**. Just add the apostrophe **after** the s.

the **teachers'** room (many teachers)
the **horses'** stable (many horses)

slides.title: Ask: one or many?
slides.text:
1. Find the owner.
2. Is there **one** or **more than one**?
3. One: **'s**. Many (ending in s): **s'**.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find the owner word.
2. Look in the text for clues: **two**, **both**, **all**, **many**, or a plural noun.
3. Find other possessives in the text that follow the same rule.

The clues tell you if the owner is one or many.

sentences.t: The students' paintings hang in the hall.
The teacher's painting hangs by the door.

example.explain:
**students'**: many students own the paintings, so the apostrophe goes **after** the s.

**teacher's**: one teacher, so **'s**.

together.passage: Our school has two football teams, one for boys and one for girls. The girls' team practises on Monday. The ___ team practises on Wednesday. The coach's whistle is very loud. Both teams' shirts are green.
together.hint: The team is for many boys, not one boy. Where does the apostrophe go for many owners?
together.good: Yes! Many boys share the team, so the apostrophe goes after the s: **boys'**.

sentences: Our school has two football teams, one for boys and one for girls.
The girls' team practises on Monday.
The coach's whistle is very loud.
evidence.stem: The answer was: boys'. Tap 2 sentences that show the same rule: many owners, apostrophe after the s.
evidence.wrong: This sentence shows one owner ('s) or no owner at all. Find sentences with s'.

checks.passage: All the ___ bags were lined up by the door.
checks.why: **All** tells us there are many students, so the apostrophe goes after the s.

checks.passage: My two sisters share a room. The ___ room is painted yellow.
checks.why: Two sisters own the room, so we write **sisters'**.

checks.passage: The nurse's office is next to the library. The libraries books are new. The principal's office is upstairs.
checks.why: The books belong to one library. It should be **library's** books.

again.title: Write the owner first
again.text: First write the owner word **without** an apostrophe. Then add the mark at the end.
again.example:
one dog → dog → **dog's** bone

three dogs → dogs → **dogs'** bones

slides.title: Plurals without s
slides.text:
Some plural nouns do **not** end in s: children, men, women, people, mice.

For these, add **'s**, just like one owner:
the **children's** playground
the **women's** club

slides.title: Names ending in s
slides.text:
For a name that ends in **s**, add **'s**.

**Yunus's** bike
**Idris's** notebook

Some writers add only **'** (Yunus' bike). Both are seen, but **'s** is common in school writing.

slides.title: Plural or possessive?
slides.text:
A plural just means **more than one**. It has **no** apostrophe.

The **players** ran onto the field.
The **players'** boots were muddy.

Only use the apostrophe when something **belongs** to the noun.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Write the owner as a plural or singular word.
2. Does it already end in s? If not, add **'s**.
3. Look for other possessives in the passage that follow the same rule.

Check plurals too: if nothing is owned, there is no apostrophe.

sentences.t: The museum has a special room for families.
The children's games are on the left.
Their parents' chairs are by the wall.

example.explain:
**children** does not end in s, so we add **'s**: children's.

**parents** ends in s, so we add only **'**: parents'.

together.passage: The city library opened a new section last month. The children's corner has soft cushions and picture books. Upstairs, the men's and women's reading rooms are quiet places to study. In the hall, a board shows ___ favourite books. Many readers have added their own ideas.
together.hint: **People** is already plural, and it does not end in s. Which rule fits?
together.good: Yes! **People** is plural but has no s, so we add **'s**: people's.

sentences: The city library opened a new section last month.
The children's corner has soft cushions and picture books.
Upstairs, the men's and women's reading rooms are quiet places to study.
In the hall, a board shows ___ favourite books.
Many readers have added their own ideas.
evidence.stem: The answer was: people's. Tap 2 sentences with plurals that do not end in s, but still take 's.
evidence.wrong: This sentence has no plural like children, men or women with 's. Look again.

checks.passage: The ___ shoes were lined up outside the classroom.
checks.why: **Children** is plural without s, so add **'s**: children's.

checks.passage: Our neighbour Abbas has a new car. ___ car is silver.
checks.why: The name is **Abbas**. To show he owns the car, add **'s** after the full name.

checks.passage: The farmers' market opens at six. Many farmer's bring fresh vegetables. The market's busiest day is Friday.
checks.stem: Which word has an apostrophe it should NOT have?
checks.why: Many farmers bring vegetables; they do not own anything here. It should be the plain plural **farmers**.

again.title: The owner stays whole
again.text: Never cut the owner word. Write the whole word first, then add the mark.
again.example:
the toys of the children → children → **children's** toys

the bike of Idris → Idris → **Idris's** bike

slides.title: Owning together
slides.text:
When two people own **one** thing **together**, add 's only to the **last** name.

**Sami and Badr's** project (one project, shared)

slides.title: Owning separately
slides.text:
When each person owns **their own** thing, add 's to **each** name.

**Sami's and Badr's** bikes (two bikes, one each)

The apostrophes change the meaning.

slides.title: Long owners
slides.text:
For a compound noun, add 's to the **last word**.

my **brother-in-law's** shop
the **head teacher's** office

For a plural compound, keep the plural inside: my **sisters-in-law's** visit.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
Apostrophes carry **meaning**, so the text must back up your choice.

1. Find the owners.
2. Look for words like **together**, **share**, **each**, **own**, **both**.
3. Decide: one shared thing or separate things?

Point to the sentence that tells you how the owning works.

sentences.t: Lina and Dana wrote one report together.
Lina and Dana's report won a prize.
Lina's and Dana's notebooks were full of notes.

example.explain:
Sentence 1 says they wrote **one** report together, so only the last name gets 's: **Lina and Dana's report**.

They each have their own notebook, so **both** names get 's.

together.passage: My aunt and uncle opened a small bakery together ten years ago. Today, ___ bakery is famous in our neighbourhood for its date cakes. Every Friday, my cousins help out. Maha folds the cake boxes, while Khalid and Salem serve customers at separate counters. Last week, a food writer from the city newspaper visited and described the bakery as a family treasure.
together.hint: Is this one bakery they share, or two bakeries? Find the word in the text that tells you.
together.good: Yes! They opened **one** bakery **together**, so only the last owner gets 's.

sentences: My aunt and uncle opened a small bakery together ten years ago.
Today, ___ bakery is famous in our neighbourhood for its date cakes.
Every Friday, my cousins help out.
Maha folds the cake boxes, while Khalid and Salem serve customers at separate counters.
Last week, a food writer from the city newspaper visited and described the bakery as a family treasure.
evidence.stem: The answer was: my aunt and uncle's bakery. Tap the sentence that proves they own it together.
evidence.wrong: This sentence does not tell us how the bakery is owned. Find the one with the word that shows sharing.

checks.passage: Faisal and Noor each painted a picture for the art show. ___ paintings were hung side by side.
checks.why: Each painted their **own** picture, so **each** name takes 's.

checks.passage: My uncle visits his mother-in-law every week. His mother-in-laws garden is full of roses.
checks.stem: How should the error be fixed?
checks.why: For a compound noun, add 's to the **last** word: **mother-in-law's**.

checks.passage: The twins share a bedroom. The twins room has bunk beds.
checks.stem: How should the second sentence begin?
checks.why: Two twins share one room. **Twins** is plural and ends in s, so add only **'**.

again.title: Draw it
again.text:
Picture the things being owned.

One thing with two owners → **one** 's at the end.
Two things with one owner each → 's on **both**.
again.example:
Ali and Hassan share one tent: **Ali and Hassan's** tent.

Ali and Hassan each have a tent: **Ali's and Hassan's** tents.
